subject: Embeddings migration + SDK/auth questions
message_1_body:
Thanks again for the call today — quick recap and a few follow-ups from our side.

Recap: we currently use Vectorly (hosted) for embeddings and a small in-house reranker. We evaluated Redwood during the demo and are interested in migrating to reduce per-query cost and get better reranking.

Open questions we want help on: 
- Recommended vector dimensionality: currently using 1024 — should we move to 1536 or 768 for better model parity?
- Batching guidance: nightly bulk ingest ~2M vectors; queries are ~100/s peak. What batch sizes are good for throughput vs latency?
- Normalization: should we L2-normalize at ingest or at query time? Any concerns for existing pipelines?
- Migration strategy: do you have a checklist for reindexing and fallbacks during cutover? We need a plan to avoid downtime for search.
- SDK / auth: we prefer using short-lived mTLS or OIDC tokens instead of long-lived API keys. Does Redwood support that?
- Routing & rerankers: can we route queries to a lightweight ANN index for recall and then call a small reranker model in the same pipeline (tool-calling/structured output) for top-K ordering?

Can you send a short migration checklist and recommended defaults so we can review internally? Also available for a 30-minute follow-up with your solutions engineer next week.

Thanks,
Sarah
Head of Search Engineering, Acme Corp
<sarah.blake@acme.com>
message_2_body:
Hi Sarah — great meeting, appreciate the details. Short answers and proposed next steps below.

Quick recommendations:
- Dimensionality: for most semantic search workloads we suggest 1536 for parity with our default model (best quality), 768 is a good compromise if you want lower storage/cost with modest quality tradeoffs. Since you're at 1024 today, we usually see an uplift moving to 1536 but it depends on your downstream model.
- Batching: for bulk ingest use batches of 5k–20k vectors (depending on memory); do multi-threaded uploads with backoff. For real-time single requests, batching at the application layer of 16–64 vectors per request often gives a good throughput/latency tradeoff.
- Normalization: L2-normalize embeddings at ingest time if you use cosine similarity for search — this avoids re-normalizing at query-time and simplifies ANN indexes. If you need dot-product (un-normalized), skip L2 but keep consistency across training and serving.
- Migration: we'll share a checklist (attached) — typical steps: export source vectors, transform/normalize, load into a staging index, run A/B traffic against old provider, then cutover with small percentage rollouts. Redfall/backout steps included.
- SDK & auth: Redwood supports API keys, short-lived signed tokens, and mTLS for Private deployments; OIDC with short-lived access tokens is available via our enterprise auth integration. We'll work with your security team on the preferred flow.
- Routing & rerankers: yes — route queries to an ANN index (fast recall) then call an internal reranker as a second call. Our API supports tool-calling/structured output so you can return candidate ids + scores then invoke a reranker model in the same pipeline or as a secondary request.

Next steps: 1) I attached a migration checklist and a small SDK snippet (Vivek will follow up with a full example). 2) Can we schedule 30 minutes for a technical deep-dive with Vivek next Thursday at 11am PT? Please confirm. 3) If you can share a sample of ~10k vectors (anonymized) and current index size, we can run a quick POC benchmark.

I'll loop Vivek on the tech details.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
message_3_body:
Hi Sarah — Vivek here (solutions engineering). Adding a few concrete notes and a quick SDK snippet to get you started. Attachments: redwood-embeddings-migration-checklist.pdf, sdk-setup-snippet.txt

Batching guidance (practical):
- Bulk ingest: 10k per request works well when you stream to our /embeddings/import endpoint; tune concurrency based on instance size.
- Real-time: group at request time to 32–64 vectors if latency budget allows. Use our async streaming API for larger batches.

Normalization:
- We recommend normalizing at ingest for cosine usage: compute L2 norm and divide each vector. Doing this once at ingest is cheaper than normalizing at query-time.
- If you keep existing 1024 dim vectors, Redwood supports custom index shapes; you can migrate without changing dims but may lose some quality improvements from model parity.

SDK/auth example (Python):
- install: pip install redwood-sdk
- auth: from redwood import Client
  client = Client(auth_type="short_lived_token", token="<token-placeholder>")
  embeddings = client.embeddings.create(model="redwood-text-embedding-1536", inputs=[...])

Routing/reranking:
- Pattern: recall -> rerank. Use the embeddings search API to return top-K ids + scores, then call the reranker model (structured function call) for the top 50. The SDK supports batch reranks as a single call.

Migration checklist (high level):
1) Export snapshots from Vectorly (CSV/Parquet).
2) Transform: map dims, normalize if switching to cosine.
3) Load to staging index and validate recall/latency.
4) Run parallel traffic (shadowing) and compare metrics.
5) Gradual rollout (5/20/100%) with automated rollback on regressions.

I'll bring a short demo for the Thursday session if you confirm the time. Also include an example cost estimate if you share current monthly query volume and index size.

— Vivek
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
